data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest protocol is an epoch-versioned intent log with an immutable, epoch-partitioned evidence store; it must durably record per-problem intent entries and epoch-commit markers.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The journal tail is corrupted or truncatable by the underlying storage medium.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The epoch marker itself is not durably fsynced before workspace mutation begins.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The evidence store allows in-place updates within an epoch, violating the immutability assumption.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Before modifying the workspace, the process durably appends an intent record to a strictly append-only journal partitioned by epochs. Evidence is written to immutable, content-addressed partitions keyed by (problem-id, epoch). When reclamation occurs after a crash with no terminal record, the protocol replays the journal tail from the last durable epoch marker; any evidence partition referenced by a committed intent is preserved, while unreferenced workspace state is reclaimed. This guarantees that completed evidence, once committed to an epoch partition, can never be silently displaced because the store is append-only and the journal provides an auditable path from crash to recovery.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
